objectives: Identify rimes in taught gl-words and familiar CVC partners.
Group words that share the vowel and ending sounds.
Distinguish words that share gl but have different rimes.
Decode each word fully after sorting.
concepts: A word family shares a rime, not necessarily an onset.
Gl-words such as glad, glob, glum and glass have different rimes.
CVC partners such as sad, blob, gum and mass help make the rime pattern visible.
Word-family sorting supports decoding but does not replace it.

definitions.definition: Words that share a rime, such as glad and sad with -ad.
The vowel and sounds that follow it in a syllable.
The initial consonant sound or group before the vowel.

workedExamples.solution: They share -ad; glad has onset gl and sad has onset s.
Both begin gl but have different rimes: -ob and -um.

commonMistakes: Grouping words by onset instead of rime.
Treating all gl-words as one family.
Ignoring the final consonant when sorting.
Guessing from the family label rather than decoding the full word.
keyTakeaways: Compare the vowel and ending to identify a rime.
Words with the same onset can have different rimes.
Words with different onsets can share a rime.
Decode the whole word after sorting.

basic.prompt: What is the rime in glob?

conceptual.prompt: What makes glad and sad a word-family pair?
Do glob and glum share a rime?
conceptual.answer: No; they share gl but have -ob and -um.

conceptual.prompt: Why should you decode after sorting?
conceptual.answer: The family pattern helps but does not replace reading the whole word.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How are glob and blob alike and different?
higherOrderThinking.answer: They share -ob; glob has onset gl and blob has onset bl.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why are glad and glob in different rime groups?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Their vowel and ending differ: -ad and -ob.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: What should you do if a word does not sound like its family?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Decode it again and check every grapheme.

mixedReview.prompt: What is the onset in glass?
What does a word-family sort help you notice?
mixedReview.answer: Shared rimes and differences among words

activities.name: Sort gl-words by rime.
steps: Read glad, glob, glum and glass.
Pair each with a familiar CVC word sharing its rime.
Name the onset and rime in each word.
Read every word again to confirm the sort.

activities.name: Compare gl-words with similar rimes.
steps: Contrast glob/glum to hear the vowel and ending difference.
Explain why the onset alone cannot identify the word.

outcomes: Identify onset and rime in taught gl-words.
Explain differences among gl-words with the same onset.
Decode the full word after sorting.
